2026.SC33.15.t: 3718 and 3730 Kingston Road - Zoning By-law Amendment - Appeal Report
2026.SC33.15.s:
This report provides updates on item SC31.2 - 3718 and 3730 Kingston Road – Zoning By-law Amendment. On June 3, 2026 the applicant appealed the application to the Ontario Land Tribunal (the "OLT") citing the failure of City Council to make a decision within the time frame legislated by the Planning Act.

Through the Decision Report submitted to Scarborough Community Council, staff recommended approval of the 24 storey building containing 419 residential units and 672 square metres of non-residential gross floor area. Scarborough Community Council considered this item and recommended that City Council refuse the application. City Council subsequently considered the item on May 21, 2026, and referred it to the July 9, 2026 Scarborough Community Council meeting to allow the proponent to finalize their proposal in conjunction with a community meeting paid for at their expense. As the applications have been appealed, the requests made of the applicant through the referral have not been undertaken.

The appealed application remains in the form previously recommended for approval by staff. This report recommends that City Council direct the City Solicitor and other staff as appropriate, attend the OLT to support the application in its current form.
2026.SC33.15.r:
The Director, Community Planning, Scarborough District recommends that:

1. City Council direct the City Solicitor, together with Development Review staff and other staff as appropriate, to attend the Ontario Land Tribunal hearing in support of the Zoning By-law Amendment application for the property at 3718 and 3730 Kingston Road.

2. City Council authorize the City Solicitor and City Staff to take any necessary steps to implement City Council's decision, including requesting any conditions of approval that would be in the City's interest, in the event the Ontario Land Tribunal allows the appeal, in whole or in part.

2026.SC33.16.t: 1891 Eglinton Avenue East - Class 4 Noise Area Classification (NPC-300) - Final Report
2026.SC33.16.s:
This report recommends that City Council classify a portion of the lands at 1891 Eglinton Avenue East as a Class 4 Noise Area under the Environmental Noise Guideline, Stationary and Transportation Sources - Approval and Planning (Publication NPC-300) ("Environmental Noise Guideline (NPC-300)") administered by the Ministry of Environment, Conservation and Parks ("MECP"). The purpose of this classification is to implement a mixed-use development on the Future Development Lands ("FDL") area identified in the Official Plan Amendment for the subject lands.

A Noise Assessment Study was prepared by Arcadis in support of the development of the FDL area on the lands at 1891 Eglinton Avenue East, which confirms that the site is suitable for a Class 4 Area classification as identified in the Environmental Noise Guideline NPC-300. This Study has been peer reviewed by a consultant retained on behalf of the City, who agrees that this site is a candidate for Class 4 Area classification.

A Class 4 Area allows for higher sound level limits than would otherwise be permitted in relation to a noise sensitive land use, such as residential dwellings and associated outdoor living areas. The impact of such higher levels is mitigated by the implementation of specified noise control measures as part of associated future development approval processes.

A Class 4 Area classification endorsed by City Council resolution would allow for existing industrial or commercial operations close to the subject site to use this noise classification and sound level limits in applications for required provincial approvals, including operation certificates.
2026.SC33.16.r:
The Director, Community Planning, Scarborough District recommends that:

1. City Council classify a portion of the lands municipally known as 1891 Eglinton Avenue East as a Class 4 Noise Area, pursuant to Publication NPC 300 (Ministry of Environment, Conservation and Parks Environmental Noise Guideline Stationary and Transportation Sources - Approval and Planning) shown as Attachment 2 to this Report.

2. City Council forward its decision on this classification to the Ministry of Environment, Conservation and Parks.

2026.SC33.20.t: Metrolinx Scarborough Subway Extension - Authority to Enter into Agreements for Temporary Retaining Walls and Other Support Structures
2026.SC33.20.s:
This report seeks City Council authority to enter into one or more agreements with Metrolinx respecting temporary retaining walls and other similar structures and installations required within the City road right-of-way for construction of the Scarborough Subway Extension (SSE) project.

Metrolinx identified several locations where temporary retaining walls are required to facilitate traffic diversions, excavation activities, and associated construction works. The temporary retaining walls will be constructed, maintained and removed by Metrolinx as part of the SSE project, with the affected portion of the road right-of-way restored upon completion of the works.

Transportation Services staff have determined that the delegated authority provisions under Chapter 743, Use of Streets and Sidewalks, of the Toronto Municipal Code do not clearly contemplate agreements for temporary retaining walls and other similar structures and installations located entirely within the public road right-of-way.

The proposed agreements will establish Metrolinx’s responsibilities with respect to the design, construction, inspection, maintenance, monitoring, insurance, indemnification, removal, and restoration of the temporary structures. The recommendations in this report authorize the General Manager, Transportation Services, in consultation with the City Solicitor, to negotiate, enter into, amend, and execute such agreements with Metrolinx.
2026.SC33.20.r:
The Acting Deputy General Manager, Transportation Services, recommends that:

1. City Council authorize the General Manager, Transportation Services, in consultation with the City Solicitor and other appropriate City officials, to negotiate, enter into, execute, amend, administer agreements with Metrolinx respecting temporary retaining walls and other similar structures and installations installed wholly within the City road right-of-way and required for construction of the Scarborough Subway Extension project, including provisions respecting design, construction, access, inspection, monitoring, maintenance, insurance, indemnification, liability, removal, restoration, and other related matters, on terms satisfactory to the General Manager, Transportation Services and in a form satisfactory to the City Solicitor.

2. City Council direct that the agreements contemplated in Recommendation 1 include indemnification and hold harmless provisions in favour of the City, on terms satisfactory to the General Manager, Transportation Services and the City Solicitor, respecting any claims (including third party claims), damages, costs, losses, and liabilities arising from or related to the temporary retaining walls and associated construction activities.

As Military Trail is classified as a collector street, City Council approval of this report is required.

Altree Developments is constructing an 8-storey purpose-built student rental at 1650 Military Trail. The site is located on the northwest corner of Military Trail and Morrish Road.

Construction will be undertaken in two phases with varying degrees of boulevard and lane closures taking place on Morrish Road and Military Trail. At the time of this report, Phase 1 (shoring and excavation) is in progress on Morrish Road. Phase 2 (building construction) will require the continuation of the occupation of Morris Road and the additional occupation of Military Trail. This report deals with the matters related to Phase 2.

2026.SC33.36.r:
The Director, Congestion and Network Management, Transportation Services, recommends that:

1. City Council authorize the closure of the north boulevard allowance and a 5.1 metre wide portion of the westbound curb lane on Military Trail, between Kingston Road and a point 72.5 metres west, from September 30, 2026, to July 31, 2028, inclusive.

2. City Council rescind the existing parking prohibition in effect at all times on the north side of Military Trail, between Kingston Road and a point 72.5 metres west.

3. City Council prohibit stopping at all times on the north side of Military Trail, between Kingston Road and a point 72.5 metres west.

4. City Council direct the applicant to pressure wash or sweep (weather permitting) the construction site and adjacent sidewalks and roadways daily, or more frequently as needed to be cleared of any construction debris and made safe.

5. City Council direct the applicant to clearly consult and communicate all construction, parking and road occupancy impacts with local business improvement areas and resident associations in advance of any physical road modifications.

6. City Council direct the applicant to provide a sufficient number of traffic control persons as determined by the Work Zone Coordinator and Toronto Police Construction Liaison Officer, on a daily basis to control construction vehicle access and egress to and from the site and maintain a safe environment for the public.

7. City Council direct the applicant to provide a sufficient number of pay-duty Police Officers as determined by the Work Zone Coordinator and Toronto Police Construction Liaison Officer, during large scale concrete pours and large-scale material deliveries to control vehicle access and egress to and from the site and maintain a safe environment for the public.

8. City Council direct the applicant to post a 24-hour monitored construction hotline number on the hoarding board, which must be prominently placed and legible from 20 metres and on all elevations from the construction site.

9. City Council direct the applicant to provide and install public art, including mural artwork, onto every elevation of the hoarding board with adequate spotlighting for night-time illumination, at their sole cost, to the satisfaction of the Ward Councillor.

10. City Council direct the applicant to provide monthly community meetings, to discuss any concerns raised by the community.

11. City Council direct the applicant to cooperate with and provide all necessary assistance to the City Engineers, staff and representatives carrying out operation, maintenance, and construction activities to municipal infrastructure with the vicinity of the construction staging area, and at no cost to the City to remove any staging to accommodate the necessary municipal infrastructure work.

2026.SC33.38.t: Morrish Road Operational Closure at Highway 2A/Military Trail - Road Alteration
2026.SC33.38.s:
Transportation Services, in collaboration with Development Review, is requesting City Council authorization to implement road alterations at Highway 2A/Military Trail as an interim measure to achieve the goals of the Highland Creek Village Transportation Master Plan (TMP). This work will comprise the following:

- The closure of the south end of Morrish Road through the installation of a cul‑de‑sac

- The closure of the Highway 2A/Kingston Road off‑ramp to Morrish Road

- Associated roadway and geometric modifications

- The delivery of pedestrian connections and landscaping on the closed portion of Morrish Road

- Required traffic by-law amendments

The TMP was adopted by City Council in May 2021 and provides the policy context for the proposed changes.

Vehicular access to/from Highway 2A/Kingston Road would be maintained via right‑in and right‑out movements at Military Trail, using the existing westbound curb lane, with all other turn restrictions remaining unchanged. The proposed road alterations are expected to enhance pedestrian safety, improve streetscape conditions, and reduce pedestrian–vehicle conflicts while maintaining acceptable roadway operations.

All design and construction costs associated with the road alterations, including public realm improvements, will be delivered by the developer of 1650 Military Trail through the Section 37 agreement.
2026.SC33.38.r:
The Director, Enforcement and Street Management, Transportation Services recommends that:

1. City Council authorize the operational closure of the south end of Morrish Road at Highway 2A/Military Trail through the installation of a cul-de-sac, and direct that all associated roadway modifications, including the physical construction of the cul-de-sac and required geometric adjustments, be implemented generally in accordance with the Highland Creek Village Transportation Master Plan and the design plans submitted in support of the development at 1650 Military Trail, as shown in Appendix 1 to the report (June 22, 2026) from the Director, Enforcement and Street Management, Transportation Services.

2. Subject to approval of Recommendation 1 above, City Council amend the existing no parking anytime restriction on the west side of Morrish Road, between Kingston Road and Old Kingston Road, to be in effect between Old Kingston Road and the south end of Morrish Road.

3. Subject to approval of Recommendation 1 above, City Council rescind the existing one‑way counter‑clockwise traffic operation on Kingston Road channelization loop, between Kingston Road and Military Trail.

4. Subject to approval of Recommendation 1 above, City Council designate the northerly westbound lane on Highway 2A/Kingston Road, between Military Trail and a point 30.5 metres east, for right-turns only, buses excepted.

5. City Council reduce the speed limit from 50 km/h to 40 km/h on Military Trail, between Old Kingston Road and Highway 2A/Kingston Road.

2026.SC33.50.t: Sheppard Avenue East at Massie Street and at a Point 390 Metres East of McCowan Road - Traffic Control Signals
2026.SC33.50.s:
As the Toronto Transit Commission (TTC) operates a transit service on Sheppard Avenue East, City Council approval of this report is required.

Transportation Services is requesting approval to remove the pedestrian refuge islands (PRI) and replace with traffic control signals at the following two locations on Sheppard Avenue East:

- At the existing PRI located approximately 10 metres west of Massie Street, to be replaced with traffic control signals at the intersection with Massie Street

- At the existing PRI located approximately 440 metres east of McCowan Road, to be replaced with mid-block traffic control signals approximately 390 metres east of McCowan Road

The two traffic control signals will provide enhanced safety for all road users and are justified based on the assessments undertaken. There are several factors for the proposed recommendations:

- PRIs do not provide right-of-way for pedestrians and are not considered an enhanced form of pedestrian crossing protection.

- The heavy traffic on the five-lane cross-sections of Sheppard Avenue East poses potential safety concerns for pedestrians crossing at the subject PRIs to access the TTC bus shelters located on both sides of Sheppard Avenue East.

- The significant distance between the nearest protected pedestrian crossings on Sheppard Avenue East at both PRI locations.

The above recommendations will provide improved accessibility and a safer and more convenient crossing of Sheppard Avenue East for pedestrians, including TTC passengers.
2026.SC33.50.r:
The Director, Enforcement and Street Management, Transportation Services recommends that:

1. City Council authorize the installation of traffic control signals at the intersection of Sheppard Avenue East and Massie Street.

2. City Council prohibit pedestrian crossings on Sheppard Avenue East, between the west curb line of Massie Street and a point 30.5 metres east of the east curb line of Massie Street, in conjunction with the installation of traffic control signals as set out in Part 1 above.

3. City Council authorize the installation of traffic control signals on Sheppard Avenue East at a point 390 metres east of McCowan Road.

4. Subject to the approval of Recommendation 1 above and in conjunction with the installation of traffic control signals at the intersection of Sheppard Avenue East and Massie Street, City Council authorize the removal of the existing pedestrian refuge island on Sheppard Avenue East, approximately 10 metres west of Massie Street.

5. Subject to the approval of Recommendation 3 above and in conjunction with the installation of traffic control signals on Sheppard Avenue East at a point 390 metres east of McCowan Road, City Council authorize the removal of the existing pedestrian refuge island on Sheppard Avenue East, approximately 440 metres east of McCowan Road.

2026.SC33.55.t: Expansion of the Free-Floating Car-Share Program into Ward 20
2026.SC33.55.s:
This staff report is about a matter that Community Council has delegated authority from City Council to make a final decision.

The report recommends expanding the Free-Floating Car-Share Program operating area into a portion of Ward 20, consistent with the expansion framework approved by City Council in October 2025. The expansion was requested by the City's sole active free-floating car-share operator in response to observed demand and has been developed in consultation with City staff and the local Ward Councillor.

If approved, free-floating car-share vehicles operating under a valid permit would be exempt from the City-wide three-hour unsigned parking limit and parking regulations imposing maximum parking periods of one hour or more within the approved expansion area. All other parking regulations would continue to apply, and existing program requirements to prevent vehicle clustering and prolonged parking would remain in effect.

The proposed expansion would increase access to one-way car-share services for residents in Ward 20 neighbourhoods located outside permit parking areas, supporting the City's objectives to enhance mobility options and provide greater transportation choice.

The Ward Councillor has been advised of the recommendation contained in this report.
2026.SC33.55.r:
The Acting Director, Street Permits, Transportation Services recommends that:

1. Scarborough Community Council amend Schedule XLVIII, Parts 1 and 2, of Chapter 950, Traffic and Parking, of the City of Toronto Municipal Code, generally as described in Attachment 1 of this report (June 17, 2026) from the Acting Director, Street Permits, to expand the Free-Floating Car-Share Program operating area into the portion of Ward 20 identified in Attachment 1.

Amended Schedule XLVIII, Parts 1 and 2, of Chapter 950, Traffic and Parking, of the City of Toronto Municipal Code, generally as described in Attachment 1 to the report (June 17, 2026) from the Acting Director, Street Permits, Transportation Services, to expand the Free-Floating Car-Share Program operating area into the portion of Ward 20 identified in Attachment 1 to the report (June 17, 2026) from the Acting Director, Street Permits, Transportation Services.

2026.SC33.59.t: Anson Avenue Area Traffic Calming and Safety Review
2026.SC33.59.s:
Safety measures are needed on Anson Avenue and the surrounding area to help ensure the safety of the community, particularly for families, children, students, seniors, pedestrians, cyclists, and other vulnerable road users travelling near Anson Park Junior Public School. Residents have raised ongoing concerns about speeding, cut-through traffic, traffic volumes, pedestrian safety, parking conditions, and school-area safety, especially during student drop-off and pick-up times when pedestrian activity is higher.

At recent community consultation, organized by my office, residents identified Oakridge Drive as an example of a nearby street where road safety measures, including all-way stop controls and traffic calming interventions, have helped address similar neighbourhood concerns. Following resident feedback, we recommend that City staff explore comparable safety improvements for Anson Avenue, including whether all-way stops, traffic calming measures, or a combination of both would be most appropriate. As part of this review, we also request that staff examine the need for potential all-way stop controls at Anson Avenue and Harewood Avenue, Anson Avenue and Allister Avenue, Anson Avenue and Dorset Road, and Randall Crescent/Dorset Road and Allister Avenue, as well as traffic calming measures on Anson Avenue, including additional signage, speed management measures, pavement markings, and other appropriate Vision Zero measures. This highlights the need …
2026.SC33.59.r:
Councillor Parthi Kandavel recommends that:

1. Scarborough Community Council request the General Manager, Transportation Services, to study the feasibility of implementing safety improvements along Anson Avenue and the surrounding area, including but not limited to speed humps, all-way stop controls, and report back to Scarborough Community Council in the first quarter of 2027.

2. Scarborough Community Council request the General Manager, Transportation Services, to review the need for additional signage, speed measurement measures, pavement markings and other appropriate Vision Zero measures, and report back to Scarborough Community Council in the first quarter of 2027.

2026.SC33.66.t: Kelsonia Avenue and Scarboro Crescent - All-Way Compulsory Stop Controls

2026.SC33.72.t: Pharmacy Avenue and Stamford Square South/Rosita Crescent - Traffic Control Signals
2026.SC33.72.s:
Pharmacy Avenue is a major north-south roadway that serves local residents, pedestrians, cyclists, transit users, and motorists travelling through the surrounding neighbourhood. The intersection of Pharmacy Avenue and Stamford Square South/Rosita Crescent has been identified through community consultation as a location where additional traffic control measures are needed to improve safety and support safer crossings.

Residents have raised ongoing concerns about vehicle speeds, traffic volumes, and the difficulty pedestrians experience when crossing Pharmacy Avenue at this location. These concerns are especially pressing given the significant number of families, seniors, children, cyclists, transit users, and other vulnerable road users who rely on this intersection to move safely through the community. A recent collision in the area has further underscored the urgent need for enhanced safety measures, including the installation of a traffic control signal at this intersection.

Through consultation with the Councillor’s office, residents expressed support for improved traffic control at this intersection to help facilitate safer pedestrian crossings, improve visibility and compliance, and provide a more predictable environment for all roasd users.

Transportation Services supports the installation of traffic control signals at Pharmacy Avenue and Stamford Square South/Rosita Crescent, as it would help address these safety concerns by providing controlled crossing opportunities, supporting vulnerable road users, and improving overall traffic safety in the neighbourhood.
2026.SC33.72.r:
Councillor Parthi Kandavel recommends that:

1. City Council authorize the installation of traffic control signals at the intersection of Pharmacy Avenue and Stamford Square South/Rosita Crescent.
